_about: 757-300, from Boeing D6-58327 Rev H 2.2.2 (page index 20): side, plan and front views on one sheet, drawn 3.6% larger than 2.2.1 (the 757-200's). Pixels of layers.py rasters at scale 20, line centres. The B752's points moved by the two plugs (plug.py: 4.064 m behind door 2, 3.048 m behind the wing, from 2.7.1's door table and the wheelbases; --scale 1.0364) and snapped onto this sheet. Scaled by the printed 54.08 m from the nose to the tail cone (as drawn: the sheet's dimension arrow reaches 0.38 m past the drawn tail cone; the plan's 54.43 m overall and span agree with the drawn ends within 0.3%). The side view is snapped on side_all.png (fills and strokes together): the belly aft of the wing and the nacelle's core are thin strokes on this sheet. The sheet draws the cabin windows (thin strokes, closed outlines); seven behind the wing's lines are placed at the drawing's own pitch. The nacelle is the PW2000's, as on the 757-200's sheet. The cockpit panes are the B752's (the same nose), moved as its points are. A plain wingtip: the document has no winglet sheet.

sources.title: Boeing, 757 Airplane Characteristics for Airport Planning (D6-58327 Rev H, December 2024), 2.2.2 General Dimensions: Model 757-300; 2.7.1 Door Clearances
sources.note: Dimensions and outlines read off 2.2.2's side, plan and front views (tools/trace/b753/), starting from the 757-200's points (tools/trace/b752/) moved by the two plugs 2.7.1's door table and the wheelbases give (4.064 m between door 2 and the wing, 3.048 m between the wing and the aft cargo door) and snapped onto this sheet, which is drawn 3.6% larger than 2.2.1; the figures are the aircraft's measurements, not a copy of the drawing. Plain wingtips (the document has no winglet sheet; United's and Delta's 757-300s fly with blended winglets, which this shape doesn't have) and the PW2000's nacelle (as on the 757-200's sheet; Condor's and Icelandair's RB211s are longer). The sheet draws the cabin windows; the seven behind the wing's lines are placed at its own pitch. Doors 1, 2, 3 (the Type I exit behind the wing), 4 and the cargo doors sit within 0.1 m of 2.7.1's table. As on the 757-200's sheet the side view draws the fuselage 4.22 m tall against the printed 4.01 m (2.2.1's figure: 2.2.2 prints no height; its plan's width is as printed): fit to it (fit_height.py; the check's +1.4% is the wing-body fairing). The front view draws the nacelle 2.35 m across where the sheet prints 2.46 m (RR) and 2.70 m (PW); kept the drawing's.
